stories.title: Conditions on US aircraft carrier at sea for more than 250 days raise alarms
stories.summary: There are reports of food shortages, broken plumbing and other potential harms aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln, which has been at sea since November.
stories.post: 📰 NEWS: Conditions on US aircraft carrier at sea for more than 250 days raise alarms. There are reports of food shortages, broken plumbing and other potential harms aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln, which has been at sea since November. Source: BBC World.
article_sentences: Concern about living conditions on a US aircraft carrier that has been deployed in the Middle East for more than 250 days is leading a US senator to demand answers from the military about the vessel and putting more pressure on the Trump administration over the Iran war.
Reports suggest US military members aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln are living with food shortages and broken plumbing and that there have been suicide attempts.
Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth on Thursday called the reports "completely misrepresented".
The carrier left San Diego in November for the South China Sea and was then sent to the Middle East ahead of the attacks on Iran in February.
No return date has been announced.

"There have been widespread reports of shortages of basic supplies, water contamination, plumbing issues, deteriorating mental health, deck safety concerns, and disruptions in the mail system, which have caused many care packages in route to the ship to be lost in transit for months," Connecticut Senator Richard Blumenthal, a Democrat, said on Thursday.

stories.title: Builder with own observatory captures solar eclipse
stories.summary: Simon Wallace, who got hooked on astrophotography in lockdown, shares his images of the spectacle.
stories.post: 📰 NEWS: Builder with own observatory captures solar eclipse. Simon Wallace, who got hooked on astrophotography in lockdown, shares his images of the spectacle. Source: BBC Science.
article_sentences: A builder who created an observatory in his back garden has said capturing and livestreaming the solar eclipse was "fantastic".
Simon Wallace became an avid follower of online astrophotographers while he was off work during Covid and now has a fully-automated rig at his home near Stowmarket, Suffolk.
On Wednesday, he spent hours setting up his mobile gear in a rural spot with a clear view of the horizon so he could livestream, external the eclipse to his followers on YouTube.
"I've not seen one like that before - I saw one in March last year, but it wasn't as much of an eclipse as this, so for me it was really quite special," he told Radio Suffolk.
"It's just an incredible thing to see - it doesn't happen very often and it's something everyone can enjoy.
"Even the weather played ball, we didn't have any clouds, it was fantastic."
Wallace said he had always been a keen photographer and had been on a learning curve with the tech involved in capturing outer space, including galaxies and nebula.
"Before I knew it I built observatory and every clear night I have to take images, it's the unwritten astrophotographers' law.
"I tend to spend several nights on one object, and get as much data as a I can - it's quite a truncated process."
Wallace had livestreamed the partial solar eclipse from his back garden in March 2025, when the moon blocked 30 to 40% of the sun.
Wednesday's event has been described as the best solar eclipse in the UK since 1999, with more than 90% of the sun being covered by the moon at its peak shortly after 19:00 BST.
